cohort: The study included 21,698,861 delivered pregnancies, comparing patients with and without hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) in a national database between 2010 and 2021.
finding: Patients with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) have significantly higher rates of severe maternal morbidity (SMM) and adverse delivery outcomes, including preterm birth, respiratory bleeding, and cerebrovascular complications, compared to those without HHT.
mod_finding: Patients with HHT were significantly more likely to have a cesarean delivery (41.0% vs. 32.9%) compared with patients without HHT.
